shine jacob Chennai, 5 November Cosmoserve Space, an Indian startup developing active debris removal (ADR) technologies, unveiled Base 1, India’s ﬁrst private and the world’s sixth facil- ity equipped with space vision effect and microgravity simulation, in Hyde- rabad on Thursday. Beyond removing space debris, it will support satellite servicing, includ- ing in-orbit repairs and refuelling. Cosmoserve also announced a $6 million seed funding round, taking its total funding to over $9 million. Japan-based Rebright Partners joined Indian investors Aranya Holdings, Naandi Ventures, AUM Ventures and Shakti VC in the round. In July 2026, Cosmoserve ﬂew its ﬁrst payload, Mission Embrace, aboard Skyroot Aerospace’s Vikram-1 rocket. It is planning to come up with the next technology demonstration mission by mid-2027 and its ﬁrst commercial mission in early 2028. This will be part of the larger road map by the Telangana government to transform Hyderabad into one of the most affordable space hubs in the world. The state is also actively plan- ning an exclusive Space City within the upcoming Bharat Future City. “Facilities like Cosmoserve’s Base 1 show exactly why Hyderabad is leading the country in space innovation. We are now home to over 30 spacetech com- panies, including India’s ﬁrst spacetech unicorn and a few more soonicorns (soon to be unicorns). They are building everything from launch vehicles and space data centres to debris removal systems and drug discovery platforms,” said D Sridhar Babu, Minister for In- formation Technology, Electronics and Communications, Telangana. The facility brings full-stack space servicing capabilities under one roof. Base 1 houses four key facilities: An Orbital Rendezvous and Capture Lab to simulate spacecraft capture operations; a Space Robotics Innovation Lab to de- velop robotic capture systems; an ISO Class 8 clean room for satellite integra- tion; and a Mission Simulation and Control Centre to manage upcoming missions. “We will start commercial op- erations by mid-2028, and this will open our doors to a global market pro- jected to reach $14.5 billion by 2030,” added Chiranjeevi Phanindra, founder and chief executive officer (CEO) of Cosmoserve Space. The funding will support Base 1, technology demonstrations and two upcoming missions. Space debris is one of the biggest challenges facing the glo- bal space industry. Of the around 28,000 satellites in orbit, nearly 10,000 are dead or non-operational. Earth’s orbit is crowded with an es- timated 68,000 debris objects smaller than 10 cm, 1.5 million fragments measuring 1-2 cm, and nearly 230 mil- lion tiny pieces ranging from 1 milli- metre (mm) to 1 cm. Even fragments just a few mm wide can pose serious risks to operational satellites, spacecraft and missions. vvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvvv More on business-standard.
